pr.title: Phase 1.1b: bind the PostgreSQL command parameters
pr.body:
Phase 1.1b, step 2: PostgreSQL binds its command parameters instead of having them written into the SQL.

> Builds on #11 (the PostgreSQL CI run). Merge #11 first; until then this diff also shows #11's commit.

**Baseline from #11:** the suite on PostgreSQL 17 gives 1,185 passed / 0 failed / 34 inconclusive / 75 skipped, the same as on the internal database. The `Tests (PostgreSQL)` run of this PR is measured against that.

## Changes

- **`PQexecParams` for every command that has parameters.**
  - `SQLStatement::ToPositionalParameters` rewrites `@NAME` to `$1`, `$2`, ... in the same single pass as #9. A name used twice gets one position.
  - It **refuses** a parameter that stands inside a literal of the query, which can't be bound. Such a query fails, with the reason in the error log.
  - Numbers are sent typed `int4`/`int8`; an unsigned 32-bit value goes as `int8`. Strings are sent untyped, so the server gives them the type of their context, as it did with the literals before.
  - Commands without parameters, including the SQL scripts, still go through `PQexec`, which can run several statements; `PQexecParams` can't.
- **`PGConnection::GetSupportsCommandParameters()` is now `true`,** so `GenerateFromCommand` no longer runs for PostgreSQL.
- **The one parameter inside a literal,** the external account's next try (`INTERVAL '@MINUTES minutes'`), now uses the `faminutes` column, like the MySQL and SQL Server queries.
- **The connection uses `PQconnectdbParams`** with separate keywords and values in UTF-8. Before, the settings were written into one connection string without escaping: a `'` or `\` in the password, or any other setting, broke it, and non-ASCII characters went through the system code page.

## Behavior change: backslashes

The old escaping doubled every `\`. Since PostgreSQL 9.1, `standard_conforming_strings` is on by default and `\\` in a literal means **two** backslashes. So on PostgreSQL every stored value with a backslash, a path for example, has been gaining backslashes each time it was saved. Values are now stored exactly as given. Values already stored keep what they have. Windows tolerates doubled backslashes in paths, which is probably why this went unnoticed.

## Tests

- `SQLStatementTester` gains three cases for `ToPositionalParameters`: positions and reuse, escaped quotes, and refusal inside a literal. They run through `RunTestSuite` on both CI databases.
- The full suite runs on PostgreSQL through the new job.
- The server builds in Release with no warnings.

Next: MySQL/MariaDB prepared statements, with a MySQL CI run.

commit.message:
Run the regression tests on PostgreSQL as well

The MySQL and PostgreSQL connections take no command parameters: their values
are written into the SQL, which the internal database - SQL Server Compact,
binding them through ADO - never exercises. The suite only ever ran on that one.

tests.yml takes a database input. With postgresql, it starts the PostgreSQL
server of the runner image after installing, and does what DBSetup does through
the COM API: creates the database and its tables, points hMailServer.ini at it,
and has the server reinitialise. build.yml runs it as Tests (PostgreSQL) next to
the existing run. The publish job does not wait for it yet; this run establishes
the PostgreSQL baseline before the parameters are bound for real.

The result and log artifacts of the external database runs carry its name, since
both runs share a workflow run and artifact names must be unique within one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bind the PostgreSQL command parameters

The PostgreSQL connection took no command parameters, so their values were
written into the SQL by SQLStatement::GenerateFromCommand. It now binds them.

A command with parameters goes through PQexecParams. SQLStatement::
ToPositionalParameters rewrites its parameter names into $1, $2, ... in one pass,
as GenerateFromCommand does, and refuses a parameter inside a literal of the
query, which cannot be bound. Numbers are sent typed int4 or int8, strings
untyped, so that the server gives them the type of their context as it did the
literals before. Commands without parameters - the SQL scripts among them - still
go through PQexec, which unlike PQexecParams runs several statements.

The one query with a parameter inside a literal, the next try of an external
account (INTERVAL '@MINUTES minutes'), now uses the faminutes column as the
queries for the other databases do.

Values are no longer escaped, which also ends a long-standing doubling of
backslashes: PostgreSQL has read \\ in a literal as two backslashes since
standard_conforming_strings became the default in 9.1, so a value such as a path
gained a backslash for every one it had each time it was saved. Values already
stored keep what they have.

The connection settings are passed to PQconnectdbParams as keywords and values,
in UTF-8. Written into a connection string, as they were, a ' or a \ in the
password or any other setting broke it, and non-ASCII characters went through the
system code page.

SQLStatementTester covers ToPositionalParameters.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Convert empty strings between UTF-8 and UTF-16 without failing

WideCharToMultiByte and MultiByteToWideChar return 0 both when they fail and when
there is nothing to convert, so Unicode::WideToMultiByte and MultiByteToWide
reported every empty string as a failed conversion. The recordsets returned early
for empty values, and queries are never empty, so it did not show - until the
PostgreSQL connection started converting each bound value: every empty one, such
as a domain without a postmaster address, stopped the command, and the PostgreSQL
run of the regression tests failed 1,221 tests in setup.

An empty input now converts to an empty output.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Regression tests: write PostgreSQL literals as standard_conforming_strings reads them

TestSetup.Escape, which tests use to write values into raw SQL, doubled the
backslashes for PostgreSQL as the server's own escaping did. Since PostgreSQL 9.1
standard_conforming_strings is on by default, and a doubled backslash in a
literal is stored doubled. It matched the server only while the server doubled
its own values too; now that it binds them, the path a test wrote no longer
matched the path the server looked for, and the two tests that put a message
file path into hm_messages directly failed on PostgreSQL.

MySQL, where a backslash in a literal is an escape by default, still has them
doubled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

issue.title: CI: run the regression tests on MySQL

repository.name: ArzoieMail
repository.description: ArzoieMail is a free, open-source email server for Windows, forked from hMailServer. It supports SMTP, IMAP and POP3, plus anti-spam, anti-virus, DKIM, SSL/TLS, backups, scripting and a COM API. Named after my daughter Arzoie and maintained in Delhi, India.

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

issue.body:
## Summary

CI now also runs the full regression suite on MySQL, alongside the internal database and PostgreSQL. The MySQL and PostgreSQL connections write command parameters into the SQL themselves rather than binding them, so each needs its own run.

## Changes

- **`tests.yml`:** the `database` input also accepts `mysql`. The new step "Move the server to MySQL" uses the runner image's MySQL 8.0:
  - creates a data directory with `--initialize-insecure`, using an options file of its own (`--defaults-file`) so none of the image's option files apply;
  - installs and starts mysqld as a Windows service on port 3307;
  - runs `CreateExternalDatabase`, `SetDefaultDatabase` and `Reinitialize`, as DBSetup does.
- **`build.yml`:** new `test-mysql` job, "Tests (MySQL)".
- **`TestFixtureBase.TearDown`:** a failed test now prints its failure message and the errors the server logged, as it happens. The console runner only prints failures at the end of a run, and a run that hits the job timeout never gets there.

## What the first runs found

1. **MySQL stopped after the setup step.** The runner ends every process a step started when the step ends, so a mysqld started with `Start-Process` was gone before the tests began. Every test then failed in setup, after about 76 seconds of `Can't connect to server on '127.0.0.1' (10061)`, and the job hit its 120-minute timeout. mysqld now runs as a service, as PostgreSQL does. The cause only became visible through the TearDown output above.
2. **Writes were slow.** By default MySQL 8 waits for two disk flushes on every autocommit write. The options file therefore turns the binary log off and sets `innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit=2`. On the Hyper-V test VM, a setting write went from 200 ms to 4.5 ms, and `API.UtilitiesTests` from 267 s to 26 s (17 s on the internal database). The database is thrown away with the runner, so durability doesn't matter.

## Verification

All three test jobs give the same result as the baseline:

| Run | Total | Passed | Failed | Inconclusive | Skipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tests (MySQL) | 1,294 | 1,185 | 0 | 34 | 75 |
| Tests (PostgreSQL) | 1,294 | 1,185 | 0 | 34 | 75 |
| Tests (internal) | 1,294 | 1,185 | 0 | 34 | 75 |

This gives a MySQL baseline for 1.1c (MySQL prepared statements). The publish job still depends only on the build and the internal-database tests.

issue.title: Bind MySQL command parameters as prepared statements (1.1c)

repository.name: ArzoieMail
repository.description: ArzoieMail is a free, open-source email server for Windows, forked from hMailServer. It supports SMTP, IMAP and POP3, plus anti-spam, anti-virus, DKIM, SSL/TLS, backups, scripting and a COM API. Named after my daughter Arzoie and maintained in Delhi, India.

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

issue.body:
## Summary

Phase 1.1c: MySQL command parameters are now **bound as prepared statements** instead of being written into the SQL. This finishes the SQL-injection work of 1.1:

| Database | Before #9 | Now |
|---|---|---|
| SQL Server Compact | Bound | Bound |
| PostgreSQL | Inlined (injectable until #9) | Bound (#12) |
| MySQL via MariaDB Connector/C (what the installer ships) | Inlined (injectable until #9) | **Bound (this PR)** |
| MySQL via Oracle `libmysql.dll` (fallback when `libmariadb.dll` is missing) | Inlined (injectable until #9) | Inlined, escaped single-pass (#9); removed in 1.4 |

## How it works

- **`MySQLStatement` (new):** prepares, binds and executes a command with `mysql_stmt_*`, then reads the result set.
  - Every column is fetched as a string, so the recordset reads the rows exactly as it reads a query's rows.
  - Buffers are sized from `STMT_ATTR_UPDATE_MAX_LENGTH`; a longer value is fetched again in full with `mysql_stmt_fetch_column`.
  - It is the only file that includes the MariaDB headers (for `MYSQL_BIND` and `MYSQL_FIELD`), through per-file include directories. The functions are still resolved at run time through `MySQLInterface`.
- **`SQLStatement::ToPositionalParameters`** can also write MySQL's `?` placeholders: one per occurrence, so a parameter used twice is bound twice. A parameter inside a literal is still refused. `SQLStatementTester` covers both cases.
- **`MySQLConnection`:**
  - `GetSupportsCommandParameters()` is true when the MariaDB client is loaded and exports every statement function.
  - `TryExecute`, and `MySQLRecordset::TryOpen`, run a command that still has its parameters as a prepared statement.
  - Error numbers map the same way as on the query path: a lost connection is retried, and a duplicate key can be ignored by the caller.
- **Unchanged:** commands without parameters (`SET NAMES`, `USE`, `SHOW`, the internal scripts) are still sent as queries.

## Tests

`API.SqlValues`, a new regression test fixture that runs on every database:
- `TestTextValuesAreStoredAsGiven` stores and reads back text that contains quotes, backslashes, comment and statement markers, `@VALUE`, `@@ID`, `?`, `$1`, LIKE wildcards and non-ASCII characters.
- `TestLogonLooksUpTheAddressAsGiven` logs on as `o'brien@example.test`. A user name of `x' OR '1'='1` must not log on.

These are regression guards rather than reproductions: since #9, MySQL's inlined values were already escaped correctly.

## Notes

- A command with parameters now takes a prepare and an execute (two round trips) instead of one query. Caching prepared statements per connection is possible later if it ever shows up in profiles.
- The `upgrade-mariadb` skill now lists the include directories in `hMailServer.vcxproj` as version-pinned, and checks the `mysql_stmt_*` exports.
